title: Trace merge authority and webhook failure isolation
description: Select a scenario to see which path is allowed to change a protected reference, which work remains asynchronous, and what an operator or developer observes.

nodes.label: Developer or bot
nodes.detail: Pushes commits or asks to merge a pull request. The request names a repository, a target branch, and an expected head commit.

nodes.label: Merge coordinator
nodes.detail: Revalidates authorization, reviews, required checks, mergeability, and the expected branch head before attempting one atomic reference update.

nodes.label: Versioned check results
nodes.detail: Stores status evidence against an exact commit SHA. A passing result for an older commit cannot authorize a newer head.

nodes.label: Git objects and refs
nodes.detail: Durably stores immutable objects, advances the protected branch reference only when the expected old head still matches, and records the committed ref transition.

nodes.label: Durable event log
nodes.detail: Publishes the durable ref journal or outbox as a versioned repository event. Consumers can replay from this boundary without rewriting repository history.

nodes.label: Fan-out workers
nodes.detail: Route the event to notifications, search, audit, Actions, and webhook delivery queues with per-consumer offsets and backpressure.

nodes.label: Customer webhook
nodes.detail: Receives an at-least-once delivery with a stable delivery ID. It can be slow, unavailable, or accept a request before the sender records success.

nodes.label: Dead-letter queue
nodes.detail: Holds deliveries that exhausted the retry policy, including the reason, attempt count, next action, and replay identity.

scenarios.label: Healthy protected merge
scenarios.summary: The coordinator validates check evidence for the exact candidate commit and atomically advances the protected reference. Only then does an asynchronous event enter fan-out.
scenarios.result: The branch advances exactly once. Search, notifications, Actions, audit, and webhooks may converge later because none of them owns repository history.

scenarios.label: Stale status evidence
scenarios.summary: Required checks passed for an older commit, but the pull-request head changed. The coordinator sees that the evidence SHA no longer matches the candidate SHA.
scenarios.result: The merge is rejected or checks rerun for the new commit. The protected reference does not move and no merge event is emitted.

scenarios.label: Target head moved
scenarios.summary: Another merge advances the target branch after policy evaluation but before this update. The compare-and-swap no longer sees the expected old head.
scenarios.result: The atomic update fails without losing the winning merge. Recompute mergeability and policy against the new target head instead of overwriting it.

scenarios.label: Webhook timeout
scenarios.summary: The repository merge and durable event succeed, but the customer endpoint times out during delivery. The external response is not part of the merge transaction.
scenarios.result: The branch remains merged. Retry with the same delivery ID and bounded backoff; the receiver must deduplicate because a timeout does not prove the first attempt was ignored.

scenarios.label: Dead-letter recovery
scenarios.summary: Repeated delivery attempts fail and the subscriber-specific job reaches its retry limit. Other consumers continue from their own queues and offsets.
scenarios.result: Operators can inspect and replay the stable delivery after the endpoint recovers. One subscriber cannot block search indexing, audit records, or other webhook destinations.
